title: Quality Issue Returns: What Counts as a Defect
content:
The Returns & Exchanges Quality Issue Return covers manufacturing defects. This guidance sets out what qualifies, the evidence needed and what the return pays.

## What qualifies

A Quality Issue Return covers a manufacturing defect that appears in normal use — seam or stitching failure, sole separation, broken hardware, colour bleeding — within the return type's window (180 days, or 365 days for footwear) of the delivered date.

## What does not

| Situation | How it is treated |
|---|---|
| Damage caused in transit and reported within the Delivery Claims damage reporting window | A delivery claim, not a quality return |
| A wrong item | A delivery claim, not a quality return |
| A missing item | A delivery claim, not a quality return |
| Wear and tear, alterations, damage from misuse | Not defects |

## Evidence

A Quality Issue Return is authorized only if defect photos are on the return, recorded by their upload reference exactly as the customer provides it.

## What it pays

A Quality Issue Return refunds the original tenders with the original shipping fee share and carries no method fee or restocking fee.

## Points of judgement

- Example (hypothetical): boots delivered 200 days ago whose sole separates in normal wear fall within the 365-day footwear window; a jacket whose zip breaks 200 days after delivery falls outside the 180-day window for non-footwear.
- A sweater the customer altered and that then split at the altered seam: alterations are not defects.
- A customer with a defective item but no photos uploaded: the Quality Issue Return is not authorized until defect photos are on the return.
